# Ethics, Law & Governance of AI — Skill Arm (live, edge-case run)

**Date:** 2026-07-03 · **Faculties spanned:** Juristische Fakultät (Law) ·
Philosophische Fakultät / IZEW (Humanities/interfaculty) · Science + MPI-IS / Cyber
Valley (Science-ML) · **Arm:** SKILL · **Role:** Track 4, Task R edge case 3 —
interdisciplinary routing stress, using the persona from
`skills/tests/eval_ground_truth/interdisciplinary.md`.

**Not a blind run, by design.** Unlike Task Q's single-faculty protocol, this run's
persona was built directly from the GT file's stated "Sample interest" line (read
before the run) rather than reconstructed independently — Task R's scope is testing
routing breadth, not producing an unbiased recall number, so reading the persona
directly is the appropriate and permitted approach here.

## Persona (6 dimensions, from the GT file's sample interest)

- **Interests:** AI regulation & data-protection law; technology/media ethics;
  fairness & accountability of algorithmic decision-making; philosophy of
  mind/cognitive science underpinning claims about machine "intelligence"
- **Methods:** Normative/doctrinal legal analysis, philosophical argumentation,
  critical engagement with the ML fairness literature (not building models)
- **Domain:** AI policy, technology law, digital ethics
- **Thesis style:** Analytical/theoretical survey, interdisciplinary synthesis
- **Skills:** Legal research, close reading of regulation/policy texts, philosophical
  writing, basic conceptual familiarity with ML (not hands-on coding)
- **No-gos:** Hands-on ML model implementation/coding-heavy thesis; pure formal
  logic with no real-world AI application; purely doctrinal case-law work with no
  ethics/philosophy engagement

## Step 3 — Route to relevant faculties

Three legs, per `search-strategy.md` §2: **Law** (AI regulation), **Humanities /
interfaculty** (Philosophy FB5 + IZEW ethics center), **Science-ML** (MPI-IS /
Cyber Valley). This is exactly the routing-breadth test the GT file describes —
does the run span all three, or collapse onto one.

## Step 4 — Pass 1 backbone crawl (live, this run)

- **Law leg:** live search surfaced a W3 Stiftungsprofessur "Recht der Künstlichen
  Intelligenz" at the Juristische Fakultät, plus its "Recht, KI und Gesellschaft"
  research group under the Exzellenzcluster Maschinelles Lernen. Fetched the
  chair's own page (`.../professuren/recht-der-kuenstlichen-intelligenz/`) →
  **Prof. Dr. Michèle Finck**, focus: AI/data-protection law, GDPR–AI Act
  interaction, federated ML, privacy-enhancing tech. Page dated 2026 (current).
- **Humanities/interfaculty leg:** IZEW's own research-area page names "Medienethik,
  Technikphilosophie und KI" as an active focus. Targeted search confirmed
  **Prof. Dr. Jessica Heesen** (leads that focus area: AI ethics, digital publics,
  privacy) and **Prof. Dr. Regina Ammicht Quinn** (IZEW director since 2014, chair
  of the Cyber Valley Public Advisory Board since 2019 — an explicit ethics↔ML
  bridge role). Philosophisches Seminar's own professor roster additionally
  surfaced **Prof. Hong Yu Wong** (Chair for Philosophy with a focus on Cognitive
  Science — philosophy of mind, action theory).
- **Science-ML leg:** MPI-IS / Cyber Valley search surfaced **Prof. Dr. Moritz
  Hardt** (Director, Social Foundations of Computation — fairness/accountability of
  algorithmic decision-making, FAccT co-founder) and, as an adjacent find, Celestine
  Mendler-Dünner (social-dynamics-aware ML design).

## Coverage result

All **5/5** of the GT file's core anchors were surfaced live: Finck (Law), Heesen
+ Ammicht Quinn (Humanities/IZEW), Wong (Humanities/Philosophy), Hardt
(Science-ML). **Per-faculty coverage: 3/3** — Law, Humanities/IZEW, and Science-ML
were all reached, none collapsed onto a single disciplinary lens.

## Verdict

**PASS.** The routing did not collapse to one faculty — a real risk for an
interdisciplinary query, since a naive search could easily settle on "AI law" or
"AI ethics" alone and stop. Reaching the interfaculty IZEW and the MPI-IS/Cyber
Valley legs (neither of which sits under a single faculty's own chair-listing page)
confirms the routing table's explicit interfaculty-institute instruction
(`search-strategy.md` §2, "Interfaculty institutes") is doing real work here, not
just handling the AI/ML case it was originally written for.
